Forecasters Expect a Busier Storm Season on the Coast

By Coastline Wire staff
October 20, 2026

The regional weather service expects between nine and twelve named storms to reach the coast this autumn, compared with an average of seven, according to its seasonal outlook released on Monday. Warmer sea temperatures in the bay are the main reason, forecasters said, along with a slow-moving pattern of high pressure further inland.

The outlook does not predict where or when individual storms will land. Instead, it gives the odds that the season as a whole will be busier than normal, which the service puts at about 70 percent this year.

Harbour masters have been asked to check moorings before the end of the month, and the coast guard will run extra drills in the two largest ports. "We would rather practice too much than too little," said a coast guard spokesperson, who asked residents to sign up for text alerts.

Farmers in the low-lying delta are also preparing. Several have moved hay and equipment to higher ground, and the local co-op has ordered sandbags early, after shortages last year left some families waiting for days.

The service will update the outlook in mid-November. Its full report, with charts of past seasons, is available on the regional weather site.
